q-4809.problem:
Given the following data for a function $f(x):$

| **$x$** | $1.1$ | $1.3$ | $1.5$ | $1.7$ | $1.9$ | $2.1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $12$ | $15$ | $21$ | $23$ | $24$ | $25$ |

$$

$$

Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=1.7$ using a central difference approximation.
q-4809.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=1.7.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=0.2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1.7) & ≈\frac{f(1.7+0.2)-f(1.7-0.2)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{f(1.9)-f(1.5)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{24-21}{0.4} \\  & =\frac{3}{0.4} \\  & =7.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

A car travels on a straight road in such a way that its position, in meters, after t seconds is given by the function f(t). The values of f(t) for different values of t are given in the table below:

t 2 4 6 8 10 12
f(t) 1 2 4 6 14 15

Approximate the velocity f′(t) at the point t=4 using a central difference approximation with step size h=2.

a
1.5m/s
b
0.75m/s
c
3m/s
d
2m/s
e
1m/s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We use the central difference approximation f′(t)≈f(t+h)−f(t−h)2h, at the time t=4 with step size h=2. This gives f′(4)≈f(4+2)−f(4−2)2(2)=f(6)−f(2)4=4−14=34=0.75.

Therefore, the velocity of the car at the instant of time t=4 is 0.75m/s.

A liquid is heated to ${150}^{∘}\text{C}$ and then left to cool. The temperature of the liquid after $t$ hours is given by $T(t).$  The graph of $T(t)$ is shown above.

Approximate the rate of change of temperature when $t=2$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
q-51404.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{T}^{′}(x)≈\frac{T(t+h)-T(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=2$ and step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(-1) & ≈\frac{T(2+1)-T(2-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{T(3)-T(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{60-120}{2} \\  & =\frac{-60}{2} \\  & =-30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of temperature at the instant of time $t=2$ is $-30{\,}^{∘}\text{C}$ per hour.

q-51402.problem:
Sam wanted to estimate the rate of weight growth of his new puppy. He took note of its weight every week, for $7$ weeks. The results are shown in the table below, where $W(t)$ is the puppy's weight (measured in pounds) after $t$ weeks from birth.

| **$t$** | $8$ | $9$ | $10$ | $11$ | $12$ | $13$ | $14$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $W(t)$ | $9$ | $10.1$ | $11.3$ | $12.4$ | $13.5$ | $14.6$ | $15.8$ |

$$

$$

Approximate the puppy's rate of weight growth $12$ weeks after birth using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
q-51402.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{W}^{′}(t)≈\frac{W(t+h)-W(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=12$ and step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{W}^{′}(0.2) & ≈\frac{W(12+1)-W(12-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{W(13)-W(11)}{2} \\  & =\frac{14.6-12.4}{2} \\  & =\frac{2.2}{2} \\  & =1.1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the rate of weight growth at the instant of time $t=12$ is $1.1\,\text{lb}/\text{week}.$
